title: Which Pair? · Pair relay
hook: Find a game, gather your friends and start playing.

knows: The group wants an activity to play together.
doesNotKnow: The setup, turn and ending for this house-rule format.

misconception: The group has to know a complicated rulebook before starting.
objective: Learn how to play Which Pair? · Pair relay with friends.

claims.text: Original house rules: The lead writes four familiar objects, with exactly two that share an agreed visible property. The lead reads the list and names the property without identifying the pair. The others identify the two objects that share the property. Form pairs. On each pair’s turn, both people make separate attempts with fresh challenges, helping only their partner. The pair earns one point only if both succeed. Each pair has two turns. Highest score wins.
claims.source: Original playable house-rule proposal; not an authoritative ruleset for a traditional game.

claims.text: For this version: 4, 6 or 8 players; materials: Paper and pencil.
claims.source: Proposed setup and player range for this activity.

recall.question: In Which Pair?, what counts as a successful turn?
options: The group ends the round before anyone plays.
The others identify the two objects that share the property.
The lead skips the turn without attempting it.
recall.why: The others identify the two objects that share the property.
